sections.heading: Is an Elastomeric Coating the Same as Silicone?

c.v: Not exactly: elastomeric names a family of flexible coatings, and silicone is one member of it.

runs.v: Every silicone roof coating is elastomeric, but acrylic and polyurethane coatings are elastomeric too. The RCMA recognizes three liquid-applied elastomeric chemistries: silicone under ASTM D6694, acrylic under ASTM D6083, and polyurethane under ASTM D6947, so a Newark Quality Roofing coating selection starts with the roof condition rather than the product. When a bid says only "elastomeric," ask which chemistry and what dry-film thickness it specifies.

sections.heading: Silicone vs. Acrylic vs. Polyurethane Coating Systems Compared

c.v: Each coating system trades one strength for another.

runs.v: Silicone coatings resist ponding water and extreme weather, give lasting UV protection, resist mildew and organic growth, and have proven performance on dead-flat roofs, and the downsides of using silicone roof coating are a higher price per square foot, faster soiling, a slippery surface when wet, and a recoat path that accepts only silicone. Acrylic is the economical choice for most flat roofs that drain and stays bright there, but it re-emulsifies in ponded areas and usually needs two coats at 50 to 60% solids. Polyurethane is the toughest of the three against foot traffic and impact, so it often serves as a base coat at walkways and equipment areas, with aromatic grades needing a UV-stable topcoat. On most local walk-ups the choice comes down to silicone for the low spots and a drainage fix before any acrylic.

sections.heading: Freeze-Thaw, Humidity, and Application Weather in New Jersey

c.v: Application weather narrows the coating season more than the calendar does.

runs.v: A water-based acrylic cures by evaporation, so it needs air near 50°F and rising, no rain in the forecast until it skins over, and falls out of season in late autumn. Moisture-cure silicone tolerates cooler, damper days, yet it still needs a dry substrate, and the roof surface should sit at least 5°F above the dew point so condensation does not break the bond. Once cured, both films flex through the freeze-thaw cycles that open seams on older local roofs, which is the point of an elastomeric coating in the first place.

faqs.q: Should I choose a silicone or an acrylic elastomeric roof coating for my East Orange building?

runs.v: Choose silicone when ponding or standing water is present, and acrylic when soiling and recoatability matter. Silicone resists permanent immersion while a water-based coating re-emulsifies under standing water, and the water-based film re-washes cleaner with rainfall while silicone loses reflectance faster, per the RCMA, Western Colloid, Henry, and Mule-Hide.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to coat a flat roof in East Orange?

On a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, the type that holds about 77% of the city's housing units, work on more than 25% of the total roof area in 12 months requires a permit from the East Orange Building Division at City Hall, 44 City Hall Plaza.
